Predict the carbon fraction

Source: R/kb_predict_carbon.R
kb_predict_carbon.Rd

Summarise the expected carbon fraction of dry mass for the population of samples the model was fitted to.

Usage

kb_predict_carbon(
  fit,
  ...,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  estimate = stats::median,
  sig_fig = 3
)

Arguments

fit

A kb_fit_carbon object.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

conf_level

A number greater than 0 and less than 1 giving the compatibility-interval level.

estimate

A function that reduces a numeric vector of posterior draws to a single estimate, such as median or mean.

sig_fig

A whole number of significant figures for summary output.

Value

A kb_predictions object: a one-row tibble with estimate, lower, and upper columns summarising the posterior distribution of the expected carbon fraction.

Details

A single estimate, pooled over the months, sites, and tissue types of the samples supplied; to estimate for a particular time of year, filter the data before fitting the model.

See also

posterior_predict() for draws of individual sample fractions.

Other prediction functions: autoplot.kb_predictions(), kb_new_data(), kb_plot_predictions(), kb_predict_biomass_canopy(), kb_predict_biomass_in_situ(), kb_predict_cover_calibration(), kb_predict_mean_weight(), kb_predict_nitrogen(), kb_predict_size(), kb_predict_weight(), kb_predict_wetdry(), predict.kb_fit_carbon(), predict.kb_fit_cover_calibration(), predict.kb_fit_nitrogen(), predict.kb_fit_size(), predict.kb_fit_weight(), predict.kb_fit_wetdry()

Examples

kb_predict_carbon(fit_carbon_sim_nereo)
#> <kb_predictions> response: carbon_fraction
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   estimate lower upper
#>      <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1    0.261 0.253  0.27
